title: Spline Interpolation
description: Linear and cubic splines, boundary conditions, tridiagonal system, error bounds.
html:
〰️ Spline Interpolation

1. Idea and Linear Splines

Instead of one high-degree polynomial (Runge phenomenon, 4.9) many low-degree pieces with smoothness at the nodes. Linear spline = polygon ($C^0$), error $\le \frac{h^2}{8}\max|f''|$, $O(h^2)$.

2. Cubic Splines

$$s \in C^2,\; s|_{[x_i,x_{i+1}]} \in \mathcal P_3: \qquad 4n = 2n + (n-1) + (n-1) + 2\ \text{(boundary conditions)}$$

  • Natural: $s''(x_0) = s''(x_n) = 0$. Clamped: $s'(x_0), s'(x_n)$ prescribed. Periodic. Not-a-knot.
  • Moments $M_i = s''(x_i)$: $s_i = y_i + b_it + \frac{M_i}{2}t^2 + \frac{M_{i+1} - M_i}{6h}t^3$, $b_i = \frac{y_{i+1} - y_i}{h} - \frac{h(2M_i + M_{i+1})}{6}$.

$$M_{i-1} + 4M_i + M_{i+1} = \frac{6}{h^2}(y_{i-1} - 2y_i + y_{i+1})$$

Tridiagonal, strictly diagonally dominant (hence uniquely solvable, $\mathrm{cond}_\infty \le 3$), Thomas $O(n)$.

Example $(0,0), (1,1), (2,0)$, natural

$4M_1 = -12 \Rightarrow M_1 = -3$; $s_0 = 1.5x - 0.5x^3$, $s_1 = 1 - 1.5t^2 + 0.5t^3$ ($t = x - 1$); $s(0.5) = 0.6875$.

3. Properties

  • Minimality: the natural spline minimises $\int(g'')^2$ (bending energy) among all $C^2$ interpolants.
  • Error $O(h^4)$ for clamped splines and $f \in C^4$ (half the step: $/16$); natural near the boundary only $O(h^2)$.
  • Splines solve the Runge problem: $11$ nodes, error $0.022$ instead of $1.9$ for the polynomial.

4. Typical Mistakes

  • Requiring only continuity instead of $C^2$.
  • Forgetting the factor $6/h^2$ in the moment equations.
  • Wrong boundary condition: natural means $s'' = 0$, not $s' = 0$.
